about: Numbers quoted from earlier work on the family, the firmware repo's notebooks 17 to 21, as those notebooks state them. Another MG90 on another board: family values, never a truth a grade of this pair is read against. No capture of that work is loaded here; every number is copied from a printed table or sentence, the notebook and the cell or section named beside it. The two entries of status stored are the exception: a pair a servo of the family has carried, printed in no notebook.

status_words.pinned: its own notebook calls it pinned
status_words.bracketed: its own notebook gives a bracket, not a value
status_words.read directly: read off a capture with no model between
status_words.open: its own notebook leaves it open
status_words.stored: a field a servo of the family has carried, quoted as stored, printed in no notebook

inventory.conclusion: the winding loop is copper; the thermometer runs on copper's handbook slope
inventory.number: DC pair 4.52 ohm at 28.6 C, 5.09 ohm at 61.5 C, ratio 1.1261 against copper's 1.1250; 0.396 %/C, 101 % of copper at the nominal temperature
inventory.status: a confirmation, not a calibration constant: 98 to 108 % across the hot reading's bracket (59.5 to 62.3 C)
inventory.caveats: one reading per temperature at one rotor angle; meter ungraded; the hot temperature is a bracket
inventory.later: stands

inventory.conclusion: nothing fixed in series worth modeling
inventory.number: fixed part at most about 0.1 ohm, 2 % of R
inventory.caveats: the meter's 10 digits sit whole in it
inventory.later: stands

inventory.conclusion: the burst's R scales a little less than DC
inventory.number: compression 0 to 2 % over 33 C; plain fit 0.365 +/- 0.022 %/C (1.3 se under copper); two quieter routes fall 1.4 to 1.5 +/- 0.3 %
inventory.caveats: each quiet route leans on a temperature-correlated choice
inventory.later: open in its own Open list

inventory.conclusion: a contact in series moves R by percents for hours
inventory.number: first two sets 3 to 4 % high, 8 to 12 C of copper, flat inside a set, gone after the 60 C hour
inventory.caveats: does not separate heat, hours, J4 or brushes
inventory.later: stands; it is why no absolute R is used

inventory.conclusion: absolute R against a stored reference is not used on a brushed motor
inventory.later: stands

inventory.conclusion: the hot bracket rests on a 720 s decay of R
inventory.later: superseded: notebook 18 reads a decay that slow as circuit excess, not heat

inventory.conclusion: can to air
inventory.number: 32.0 +/- 0.1 C/W, 31.4 to 32.1 across the anchored rows; 29.7 and 31.2 by the heater's power, 34.9 and 36.5 by wall-clock power
inventory.caveats: per watt of winding heat with the shaft moving; the free heaters put 10 to 30 % more heat in than i^2 R; the locked hold reads 26 C/W; the bead reads between can and air
inventory.later: notebook 19 agrees on two holds, 30.89 and 32.38

inventory.conclusion: the slow mode
inventory.caveats: the 0.25 W block's can is faster up and slower down than the network (172 against 123 s, 107 against 168 s)
inventory.later: stands; notebook 21's dev-board leak wants 78.2 s

inventory.conclusion: a fast mode is in the can data
inventory.number: 17 to 24 s (20.05 anchored)
inventory.status: pinned as a product only: the can does not split R from C
inventory.later: stands

inventory.conclusion: winding to can
inventory.number: 28 +/- 3 C/W with 1.3 +/- 0.5 J/C by the fit; 40 to 45 by the bursts; 27 to 32 by the hold's curve (tau 56 to 75 s, 2.1 to 2.4 J/C)
inventory.status: bracket 28 to 45; "the fit's standard error is not the uncertainty"
inventory.caveats: the bursts are cross-seat ratios read about 8 s late (2 % of R, 5 C a run); the hold was taken in the excess state and its excess fell from 7 to 4 C at constant power
inventory.later: notebook 21 reads 13.0 to 21.0 directly; not the copper's own node (section 4 here)

inventory.conclusion: winding over air
inventory.number: 60.0 anchored, 57.1 to 71.4 across the rows
inventory.caveats: linear only over 0.25 to 0.42 W; the 1 W point was never taken
inventory.later: notebook 21 reads 40.4 to 45.6 over the room at a hold's end

inventory.conclusion: winding heat capacity
inventory.number: 1.3 J/C, "a few grams of copper and iron"
inventory.later: superseded as a statement about the copper: the copper's own node is ten times lighter (section 4 here, with stage 2's teardown and rest-resistance)

inventory.conclusion: the 0.42 W block's bursts are not a thermometer
inventory.number: 4 to 16 % over copper, climbing with the can flat
inventory.status: a finding; cause in the circuit
inventory.later: stands

inventory.conclusion: the contact-state rule
inventory.number: re-baseline after heavy running: 15 min rest, V/I flat within 2 % over three bursts
inventory.later: never graded

inventory.conclusion: predictions
inventory.number: at the 0.253 A limit the winding settles at 46 to 51 C, can 37; a hard stall at 7.43 V (11.6 W) crosses 130 C in 12 to 17 s
inventory.caveats: enamel class assumed, bridge left out
inventory.later: the stall time has no copper node in it (section 4 here)

inventory.conclusion: the family pair
inventory.number: tau 128 s, g 63 C/W over the board NTC
inventory.later: superseded by notebook 21

inventory.conclusion: a resistance is only good against itself at one seat
inventory.number: seat references spread 1.96 to 2.69 % (5 to 7 C) at one stop; anchors 3.71 %; a moved stop 9 % over the stored R
inventory.later: stands; section 2 here has mg90-d's own spread

inventory.conclusion: the bridged state
inventory.number: three references about 20 % low (-18.7 to -20.9 %)
inventory.later: stands; section 2 here has mg90-d's bridged seats

inventory.conclusion: the board NTC rests over the can
inventory.number: 2.03 to 2.75 C, moving 0.7 C between rests
inventory.status: does not say which sensor is off
inventory.later: stands; notebook 21 carries it (2.74 C)

inventory.conclusion: can over air
inventory.number: 30.89 and 32.38 C/W on two 480 s holds
inventory.later: stands

inventory.conclusion: the winding over the can at a hold's end
inventory.number: about 7 C by the host clock, none by the meter's own clock
inventory.status: "the data does not settle it"; decides whether g is about 31 or about 40 C/W over the NTC
inventory.later: open; it is the low and the high reading of section 4 here

inventory.conclusion: no heating rises faster than about 1 C in one second
inventory.number: other holds' largest one-second rise 0.46 to 1.07 C at 0.29 W
inventory.later: consistent with the copper node of section 4 here, read past its 1 to 3 s reference

inventory.conclusion: the estimator itself: gate, reference window 1 to 3 s, tracker, carry, guards, boot prior
inventory.number: carry over-reads 240 s gaps by +0.05, +1.36, +2.12 C; boot prior 6.3 C high at first
inventory.later: retired: notebook 21 replaces the resistance thermometer with the I2t heat

inventory.conclusion: rest resistance has no single value
inventory.number: 15 hand stops 4.31 to 5.30 ohm, median 4.46; 20 settles after drives 4.63 to 5.18, median 4.76; bulk 2 to 2.4 % wide, worst stop 21 %
inventory.status: a finding; one-sided or two-sided not decided
inventory.later: stands

inventory.conclusion: it shifts between sessions and relaxes after a drive
inventory.number: +0.30 ohm [0.20, 0.38] between sets; every settle falls 0.051 +/- 0.005 ohm plus 0.153 +/- 0.018 of its excess within 60 s
inventory.status: "an observation, not a finding"; film or thermoelectric voltage
inventory.later: open

inventory.conclusion: a thermometer must take R as a ratio to its own reference at the same seat and state
inventory.later: stands

inventory.conclusion: temperature
inventory.number: nothing logged; "heat killed" has no script behind it

inventory.conclusion: form
inventory.number: heat += (i^2 - heat) >> s every 16 ms; T = T_ntc + k x heat; the leak an octave of the 16 ms period
inventory.later: stands as a form; section 7 here runs two such heats on a warmed input

inventory.conclusion: NTC on the can
inventory.number: free leak 12.8 to 32.6 s; 16.4 s octave; k 0.00478 to 0.00771 cC/count^2, 13.0 to 21.0 C/W; within 3.6 C either way
inventory.later: two brackets stand

inventory.conclusion: NTC on the dev board
inventory.number: free leak 78.2 s, run at 65.5 s; k 0.01591, 43.3 C/W; 0.4 C cold, 4.3 C warm, 2.74 C of the warm side the rest offset
inventory.later: stands as that board's fit

inventory.conclusion: the copper over the room at a hold's end
inventory.caveats: under notebook 18's 57.1 to 71.4; a negative contact drift would make it low
inventory.later: open

inventory.conclusion: the excess over the can peaks early and falls back
inventory.number: 6.9 C at 34 s, 6.7 at 72 s, 9.1 at 70 s, then 2.7 to 4.6 C at the end
inventory.status: "a two-node plant does not do that"
inventory.caveats: contact steps up to 1.44 % of R, 3.7 C, in one second
inventory.later: open

inventory.conclusion: the first seconds
inventory.number: 2 to 10 s rise 1.10, 3.17, 0.29 C; capture-2 is over what 1.3 to 0.7 J/C allows
inventory.status: open: contact, the reference window, or "a heat capacity under the bracket"
inventory.later: the third candidate is now supported: the copper's own node is ten times under the bracket (section 4 here)

inventory.conclusion: proposed band
inventory.number: 5 C either way
inventory.caveats: "the real protection margin sits in i_cont itself"

inventory.conclusion: octave rule
inventory.number: a written tau runs up to 1.5 times shorter; cap 262 s
inventory.later: section 7 here takes the cap at 524 s

not_carried: Notebook 20's motor constants (Ke, J, R in rotation, breakaway) are mg90-a's and are not quoted; stage 2 holds the type values on mg90-b and mg90-c.
